subject: APAC data jurisdiction affirmation & private peering checklist
messages:
From: Alice Choi <alice.choi@tidebank.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0800
Subject: APAC hosting confirmation + CAIQ/SIG items

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — TideBank is keen to validate regional controls before we proceed with a pilot. Security has a short list:

- Formal affirmation of APAC-only hosting for our tenant (compute and persistent storage)
- VPC/private peering options and whether traffic egress can be restricted to our peering endpoint
- KMS key locality (can CMKs be created and retained in APAC only?)
- A completed CAIQ/SIG snapshot for the most recent controls we discussed

Can you provide a short statement and any evidence (network diagram, runbook, checklist) we can include in our procurement packet? Also please highlight any caveats (fallbacks to global regions, replication for DR, or logging egress).

Preferred timeline: we need the packet by EOD Thu Apr 21 to sync with our procurement window.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Choi
Senior Information Security Manager, TideBank
[Attachment: TideBank_Request_Form.pdf]
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Choi <alice.choi@tidebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:04:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC hosting confirmation + CAIQ/SIG items

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on timing and can deliver an evidence packet by EOD Thu Apr 21. Quick summary up front:

- APAC-only hosting: Redwood can pin your tenant to APAC regions (Singapore and Tokyo currently) for primary compute and persistent storage. We will not replicate customer data to other regions unless configured as part of a DR runbook.
- VPC / private peering: We support VPC peering (private link) with single-tenant private endpoints. Egress can be restricted to the peering connection and we support IP allowlists and routing policies.
- KMS locality: Customer-managed keys are supported via KMS integrations; CMKs can be created in the APAC key region and we can surface an attestable configuration in the runbook.
- CAIQ/SIG: we will attach an updated control snapshot and a short narrative for the items you called out.

I'll attach a draft runbook and a checklist for the peering steps. Marissa / Irene — can you review the runbook for any missing audit artifacts (esp. audit log retention and packet capture policy) and add the CAIQ export?

Next steps:
1) Marissa to add CAIQ/SIG PDF and confirm SOC 2 scoping line items.
2) Irene to validate KMS key locality wording and DR replication caveats.
3) Marcus to assemble packet and upload to the shared Drive link below.

We will include: runbook, network diagram, VPC peering checklist, and CAIQ/SIG snapshot.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: apac_hosting_runbook_v1.pdf]
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, alice.choi@tidebank.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:28:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC hosting confirmation + CAIQ/SIG items

Thanks Marcus — attaching the CAIQ/SIG export and a short answers doc. Key notes I added in the CAIQ narrative:

- We selected the controls most relevant to data locality and network controls (CCM-1, N-1 family, SC-2/3 equivalents) and documented where evidence lives (audit logs, config repo links).
- SOC 2: scope includes production inference runtime, control plane operations for tenant isolation, and the private peering mechanism; excluded components (e.g., some third-party CDN logs) are called out.
- Audit logs: retention is 13 months by default for enterprise customers; can be extended via an add-on.

Attachments:
- caiq_sig_responses_20270421.pdf (CAIQ export + one-page narrative)
- vpc_peering_checklist.xlsx (step-by-step with test commands and expected traceroutes)

Alice — Irene will confirm the KMS wording and any DR replication triggers. If you need us to swap the support contacts for local APAC ops, we can add that in the packet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Security Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachments: caiq_sig_responses_20270421.pdf, vpc_peering_checklist.xlsx]
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, alice.choi@tidebank.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:40:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC hosting confirmation + CAIQ/SIG items

Adding KMS and DR clarifications:

- KMS: We integrate with region-specific KMS (cloud provider CMKs). For private deployments we can also support customer HSMs via our KMS adapter. The documentation now explicitly states that CMKs created for TideBank will be provisioned and stored in the APAC key region and keys will not be exported outside the region.
- DR / replication: Primary replication for resiliency within APAC is supported (Singapore <-> Tokyo for cross-zone HA) but cross-region replication to other continents is opt-in and requires documented authorization. The runbook includes the DR failover decision flow (who authorizes, expected RTO/RPO).

I've updated the runbook to call out the audit evidence paths (CloudTrail-style logs, VPC flow logs, peering audit events) and included minimal sample log snippets.

Uploading final runbook and pushing to the Drive folder Marcus referenced.

Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: apac_hosting_runbook_v1.pdf]

Marcus / Marissa / Irene — thanks, this packet looks good and addresses our primary concerns. A few follow-ups before procurement sign-off:

1) Can you provide a signed statement (PDF) on company letterhead that the tenant will be pinned to APAC regions and that CMKs for TideBank will remain in APAC?
2) We may request extended log retention during the pilot — what is procurement pricing for +12 months?
3) We'd like a short remote test window to validate peering (30–60 min) with your ops team next week. Preferred times: Apr 26–28 (APAC mornings).

If you can get the signed letter and pricing by Fri Apr 23, procurement will proceed with the pilot paperwork next week.

Best regards,
Alice
